thread:
maria: Quick question—planning to update our envelope strategy for multi-cloud KMS. Thinking about caching DEKs with a short TTL (15m) per host and KEKs only used for wrap/unwrap, but want to balance KMS call volume, RBAC, and audit fidelity. Any obvious gotchas?
kevin: short answer: DEK caching reduces KMS pressure but increases blast radius if host compromised. How many decrypts/sec do we expect?
anna: We're seeing ~1200 decrypt ops/min at peak for hosted API. That pattern is bursty by tenant.
maria: ok that's... a lot. If we cache DEKs per-host with 15m TTL and LRU size 5000, estimate calls drop ~90%. But we need RBAC to limit which services can unwrap KEKs. Thoughts on service principals vs per-cluster roles?
devsec: prefer per-cluster roles + attribute-based access (tags) so we can revoke at cluster-level. Service principals are OK but harder to rotate at scale.
kevin: +1. Also enable KMS request logging -> send to audit pipeline. For GCP KMS, log AdminActivity and DataAccess. For AWS, CloudTrail KMS events and CloudWatch Insights.
anna: audit volume will spike if we log every decrypt. We might log unwrap/wrap (KEK ops) only and aggregate DEK usage counters.
maria: proposal: record KEK wrap/unwrap events as audit-log entries (full detail), and emit DEK cache-hit metrics (no per-request PII), with sampling for detailed DEK decrypt logs (1%). That keeps compliance signal without exploding logs.
devsec: sounds reasonable. Make sure sampled logs include request id, tenant id hashed, key id, and reason.
kevin: also add deterministic backoff on KMS throttling and a local in-memory jittered retry. For cross-cloud, centralize a small KMS client library to apply caching, RBAC checks, and audit hooks.
anna: question: for rotate DEK frequently (daily), caching 15m still ok? rotation would invalidate cached DEKs.
maria: yes rotation strategy matters. We can version DEKs: store {dek_id, dek_wrapped}. When DEK rotates, code tries local cache for active dek_id, if missing, fetch unwrap from KMS. Old DEKs kept readable for short period for in-flight requests. We need invalidation propagation.
sre-bot: deploy-notice: will run a canary of the cache library on staging tomorrow 03:00 UTC :eyes: 
kevin: For incident response, have playbook: if KEK compromise suspected -> revoke KMS key policy, rotate KEKs, mark all DEKs as expired, force rewrap flow. That will trigger mass unwraps; ensure quota for emergency rewraps.
devsec: add a 'throttle-safe rewrap' background worker that rewraps with controlled concurrency across regions to avoid KMS rate limits.
anna: vuln triage Q: if a host-level cache is stolen, what's risk? Answer: attacker can decrypt documents encrypted with cached DEKs until TTL. Mitigations: shorten TTL, bind DEK to host TPM or KMS-protected HSM, enroll host in key-wrapping attestation, or use per-tenant per-host DEKs.
maria: action items:
- implement central KMS client lib with caching, RBAC hooks, audit emitter (kevin)
- add sampling for DEK decrypt logs and KEK full logs (devsec)
- design rotation invalidation protocol (anna)
- canary deploy library on staging and monitor cache-hit vs KMS calls (sre)
kevin: I'll own the client lib PR. Also will add a configurable cache_ttl and cache_size, default 15m/5000.
devsec: I'll draft the audit schema and sample retention policy: KEK unwrap logs kept 7 years, sampled DEK decrypt logs 90 days.
anna: I'll write the invalidation doc and runbook for emergency KEK rotation.
maria: thanks team. If no objections I'll open RFC and roadmap ticket.
kevin: no objections from me. :thumbsup: 
devsec: :+1: 
audits: noted. Will reserve audit storage and check compliance constraints for EU data before rollout.
